nodes.label: DnsResolutionCarrier
nodes.responsibility: Provide bounded DNS query resolution and upstream resilience using mature dnsproxy in explicit host or consumer network namespaces, without making provider health, reachability or DNS cache contents a general connectivity guarantee.
nodes.authority: Network DNS carrier configuration and observed query response only; external resolver truth remains provider-owned
mustNotOwn: HTTP/SOCKS proxy policy or full-IP tunnel effects
acceptance: dnsproxy systemd service binds configured listening interface, port, parallel upstream and cache without taking over the host network namespace.
Dedicated upstream-resilience acceptance distinguishes partial upstream failure, valid cached answer, uncached SERVFAIL, cache expiry, and recovery without process restart.
Consumer-specific Browserless DNS service uses its own namespace and its WireGuard dependency; this is a declared configuration relationship, not installed runtime equivalence.
inputs: DNS query, selected resolver upstream configuration, namespace and cache policy
outputs: observed DNS answer/rcode or transport failure under bounded timeout
nodes.behavioralContract: Within its configured namespace and active process instance, DNS carrier forwards queries to declared upstreams, can serve qualifying cache entries, and does not report an uncached successful resolution when all upstreams fail. The named acceptance script is a scoped negative/positive witness, not a proof for all remote DNS providers.
environment: isolated Browserless network namespace variant; installed versions and active instance UNKNOWN
effects: local DNS socket listener, upstream DNS requests and bounded DNS cache effects; no arbitrary host-wide default route changes

nodes.label: ProxyTunnelTransportCarrier
nodes.responsibility: Realize separately replaceable proxy/direct transport and optional namespace-isolated TUN/full-IP traffic using mature sing-box, with exact configuration and observed connectivity instead of interpreting process health as traffic success.
nodes.authority: Network transport configuration and bounded namespace-specific connectivity witness; does not own consumer business reachability claims
mustNotOwn: independent installed service currentness from source declarations
acceptance: Direct sing-box service requires the configured DNS service, checks its config before start and uses unprivileged service account.
Optional full-IP/TUN uses a dedicated network namespace, with per-namespace link/routing checks, actual TCP connectivity and HTTP/3 traffic evidence; process/listener alive alone is insufficient.
Absence of TUN device, capability, endpoint or verified installed service remains UNKNOWN/NOT_ADMITTED, not implicitly converted to an available transport.
inputs: selected transport profile/config, DNS prerequisite, assigned namespace, accepted network permissions
outputs: configured sing-box proxy/direct or isolated TUN transport endpoint plus observed bounded connectivity/acceptance status
nodes.behavioralContract: A configured transport may be admitted only within its declared namespace and mature sing-box configuration. Default direct proxy depends on dnsproxy; optional isolated TUN shall not silently replace host-wide routes. Full-IP/QUIC qualification requires actual IP-family, TCP and HTTP/3 witnesses according to the existing scoped scripts rather than a process liveness check.
environment: isolated Linux netns optional TUN/QUIC acceptance; production install and provider availability UNKNOWN
effects: opens bounded proxy/TUN sockets, namespace routes and carrier-specific traffic; authorized physical side effects require native operator/runtime authority

slices.objective: Falsify indirect egress and DNS/control-plane bypass assumptions from real Linux, Windows, WSL and developer-tool consumers.
acceptance: Every sampled path states its DNS resolver, proxy/tunnel, actual egress destination and independent observation.
A precompromised inner execution layer still cannot access an undeclared external endpoint through metrics/auth/package services.
VPN reachability is not accepted as network policy enforcement; failure and recovery are consumer-tested.

Current supply-chain/ready.sh only emits READY when same-attempt proxy CONNECT=403 is observed. That is a conservative source-path sufficient check, NOT a necessary/provider-general meaning of policy rejection: installed sing-box can reject after CONNECT=200 and TLS reset without forwarding. Arbitrary curl failure, 407, 000, or origin HTTP403 remains insufficient.

Before admitting another native denial signature to READY, bind the exact loaded proxy policy and an independent upstream no-forwarding witness to the same source, destination and attempt. No generic curl35/HTTP000 or HTTP CONNECT alone is an allowed authority.
